name: ci

on:
  pull_request:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read

        with:

content.text: GitHub restricts the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` to read-only for `pull_request`-triggered runs on fork PRs, no matter what permissions the workflow requests — so a plain `pull_request` job can't post comments or apply labels on fork PRs. I'll use `pull_request_target` instead (runs with base-repo permissions) but without checking out any fork code, which avoids the classic "pwn request" risk since nothing from the fork is ever executed. Let me check for a real pinned SHA for `actions/github-script`.

input.content:
---
name: triage

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Welcome and label new pull request
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      # No checkout step: this job only reads data from the pull_request_target
      # event payload, so fork-submitted code is never fetched or executed.
      - name: Welcome contributor and apply needs-triage label
        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
        with:
          script: |
            const pr = context.payload.pull_request;

            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: pr.number,
              body: `Welcome, @${pr.user.login}! Thanks for opening "${pr.title}". This pull request has been marked for triage.`,
            });

            await github.rest.issues.addLabels({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: pr.number,
              labels: ["needs-triage"],
            });

# triage-demo

A repository that runs its tests on every pull request.

## Contributing

Open a pull request. Contributions arrive from forks.

## Workflows

### CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

Runs the test suite (`make test`) on every pull request.

### Triage (`.github/workflows/triage.yml`)

Runs when a pull request is opened, including pull requests opened from a fork. It:

- Posts a comment welcoming the contributor by their username and summarizing
  the pull request by repeating its title.
- Applies the `needs-triage` label.

Fork-submitted pull requests only ever get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` under the
`pull_request` event, so this workflow uses `pull_request_target` instead,
which runs with the base repository's permissions and lets it comment and
label fork PRs. It never checks out or executes the pull request's code — it
only reads the title and author from the event payload — so it isn't exposed
to untrusted code from the fork.

Added `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and updated the README. Summary:

- **Workflow** (`.github/workflows/triage.yml`): triggers on `pull_request_target` (`opened`), with `permissions: {}` at the top and `pull-requests: write` scoped to the job only. It uses `actions/github-script`, pinned to a real commit SHA for v9.0.0, to post a welcome comment (`@username` + PR title) and apply the `needs-triage` label.
- **Fork safety**: `pull_request` runs from forks always get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, regardless of the `permissions:` block, so commenting/labeling would silently fail. `pull_request_target` runs with base-repo permissions instead — the workflow never checks out or executes the fork's code (it only reads `context.payload.pull_request` from the trusted event payload), avoiding the "pwn request" risk that normally comes with `pull_request_target`.
- **README**: added a "Workflows" section documenting both `ci.yml` and the new `triage.yml`, explaining the fork-safety rationale.
